$comment: Shot list for the portfolio. See screenshots/README.md. Viewports: desktop 1440x900, phone 390x844, both at 2x. Every shot needs alt text before it can be imported.

fleet-pulse.note: Hosted demo with synthetic data. Each shot is one panel, picked by its heading, so images show the data rather than the page header. Update baseUrl if the Netlify site is renamed. Panels with wide tables use a 1920 px window; the capture warns if a table is still cut off.

shots.alt: Executive headline numbers for the month to date: revenue and energy against budget, the month-end forecast and capacity online.
shots.caption: Executive: the month at a glance, against budget.

shots.alt: A waterfall chart bridging budgeted revenue to actual revenue, splitting the gap into weather and operational causes.
shots.caption: Budget to actual: how much of the gap was weather, and how much was operations.

shots.alt: Cumulative revenue for the month plotted against the P50 budget line, with a forecast to month end.
shots.caption: Revenue against a P50 budget, with a month-end forecast.

shots.alt: Map of solar and battery sites across Canada and the US, each circle sized by the revenue the site has lost.
shots.caption: Asset manager: the fleet map, circles sized by lost revenue.

shots.alt: Breakdown of lost revenue by cause: inverter outages, curtailment, soiling, and offline or degraded strings.
shots.caption: Where the revenue went, by cause.

shots.alt: Recommended actions for the asset manager: which sites to wash and which faults to investigate, with what each is worth.
shots.caption: What to do next: wash, wait or investigate, priced in dollars.

shots.alt: Heatmap of the performance index for every site and day of the selected range.
shots.caption: PV engineer: performance index for every site and day.

shots.alt: For each site, the gap between expected and actual energy split into loss causes, including the part the model can't explain.
shots.caption: Where each site's shortfall goes, including what the model can't explain.

shots.alt: The operations dispatch queue: equipment problems ranked by revenue at stake per day, marked as still down or recovered.
shots.caption: Operations: the dispatch queue, ranked by revenue at stake.

shots.alt: One site's daily losses to soiling shown alongside daily rainfall.
shots.caption: One site: soiling losses against rainfall.

shots.alt: The operations view's headline numbers on a phone: problems to act on now with the revenue at stake, inverters down, strings offline and inverters not reporting.
shots.caption: The dashboards work on a phone too.

studio-simulator.note: The /demo page is public and has no student data. Signed-in views are left out on purpose; add them only from a demo game instance.

shots.alt: Studio Simulator's public demo page, introducing the semester-long game studio simulation.
shots.caption: The public demo page.

shots.alt: The whole demo page, including the guided tour of how a week in the simulation works.
shots.caption: The guided tour walks through a week of the simulation.

shots.alt: The Studio Simulator demo page on a phone.

step-contest.note: Taken by hand from a demo contest (Alex, Blake, Dev and Avery are demo accounts). Log steps is left out until its button stops covering the date field; contest settings is left out because it shows a live invite code; the full-page captures are too tall for the gallery.

shots.alt: A step contest on a desktop screen: a button to log today's steps, then standings for five people with their step totals, best days and how far each is behind the leader.
shots.caption: The leaderboard: totals, best days and the gap to the person ahead.

shots.alt: The contest leaderboard on a phone, ranking five walkers by total steps with each person's best day and their gap to the leader.
shots.caption: The leaderboard updates the moment anyone logs.

shots.alt: The contest activity feed on a phone: each day's entries with step counts, a short note, reactions and comments.
shots.caption: The feed keeps the group talking.

shots.alt: My log on a phone: total steps, daily average, rank and streak, a bar chart of steps per day, and the days still missing an entry.
shots.caption: Missed days are listed, so you can catch up.

shots.alt: Creating a contest on a phone: name, description, start and end dates, time zone, maximum participants and catch-up days.
shots.caption: Setting up a contest: dates, time zone and catch-up days.

shots.alt: My log on a desktop screen: total steps, daily average, rank and streak above a bar chart of steps for each day of the contest, with a dashed line at the average.
shots.caption: Every day of the contest at a glance.

daric.note: Private household app, taken by hand. Only screens with nothing personal on them are published. The others show real names, photos, notes or body weight; recapture them with names swapped (screenshots/redactions.local.json) before taking them out of skip.

shots.alt: Daric's garden module on a phone: this week's garlic planting steps for the coming season, under a photo of garlic bulbs ready to plant.
shots.caption: The garden module plans the season week by week.

shots.alt: A garlic growing guide for southern Ontario on a phone: what to do right now, when roots will form, and a button to start this year's crop.
shots.caption: Growing guides are written for our climate zone.

shots.alt: Daric's settings on a phone: a switch for each module on the home screen, including Today, Groceries, Hardware, Tasks, Notes, People, Gym and Weight.
shots.caption: Each phone chooses which modules it shows.

hexploration.note: Unity: capture in the editor or a build (Game view screenshot or Unity Recorder), save PNGs into screenshots/inbox/hexploration/ with these names, then write the alt text.
